_comment: Real #alerts-devops (C909ZH4ET) messages, captured 2026-08-24. These are the
regression fixtures for alert_parser.py — every one of them broke the parser
that had been written against guessed formats.
What real cards do that guessed ones did not:
- INCIDENT_NAME is the incident NUMBER ('119881'), not the title.
- The title lives in the attachment's linked heading, after '|Incident #N>: '.
- metadata keys inside the ``` fence are lowercase (monitoring_tool,
entity_display_name, state_message) while the VictorOps ones are upper.
- The env/name separator is ' : ', not ' - ', and Alertmanager lines can
- PandoLogic lines carry TWO parenthesised groups: labels, then the URL.
- state_message is often just '*Alertmanager:* <url>' — no time window.
- The link a human posts in #comms-noc is the VictorOps PORTAL url.
Text is verbatim; nothing is sanitized because this repo already holds
production credentials and reads these channels live.
The 'firing ALB' case is the plain positive: a VictorOps incident that is FIRING, not auto-resolved, and not on the suppression list — i.e. the one shape that must actually open a thread.
